# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which states that when the cycling light is yellow, the green wire must be cut. However, I can only communicate with Deaf via gestures, and Blind cannot see gestures or colors. 

Deaf can see the bomb and can speak to both Blind and me, but Deaf cannot hear speech. Currently, no sign convention has been established between Deaf and me ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). Deaf will observe the bomb and speak at the end of Round 1, describing the bomb's state and setting up or allowing us to establish a protocol. Any gesture sent right now would be ungrounded and meaningless.

Therefore, the best course of action is to wait for Deaf's first report.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf speaks next and will describe the bomb. Check your manual once Deaf speaks. When you know which wire to cut, gesture directly to me with N gestures for wire N (1 gesture for wire 1, 2 gestures for wire 2, 3 gestures for wire 3). I will receive N blanks and cut wire N. You can also gesture the number to Deaf so Deaf can confirm aloud.
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS: Display shows [0]. Light is [yellow]. Wires: 1 is [blue], 2 is [red], 3 is [green]. MUTE: gesture to me what Blind must do. ☝ = cut wire 1, ✌ = cut wire 2, 🤟 = cut wire 3, 👍 = press/submit, 👎 = abort/wait. I will speak your instruction directly to Blind.

The defusal manual specifies that the green wire must be cut when the light is yellow, but notes that the light changes every round in a cycle of five colours. 

In Round 1, Deaf observed the light was yellow and wire 3 is green. Since the light changes every round, Round 2 will have a different light color, making an immediate cut invalid. Deaf defined the gesture convention `👎 = abort/wait`. By signaling `👎` to Deaf (and sending nothing to Blind), Blind will not cut, allowing us to track the light's color cycle until yellow returns.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute gestured NO / WAIT / DO NOT DO THAT. I cannot hear you, so speak your observations and questions directly to Mute; Mute will gesture the answers to me, and I will speak them to you. BOMB UPDATE: Light has changed to BLUE. Display is [0]. Wires are 1:[blue], 2:[red], 3:[green]. MUTE: Use 👍 for YES, 👎 for NO/WAIT, ☝ for 1/Wire 1, ✌ for 2/Wire 2, 🤟 for 3/Wire 3, 👉 for press, 🤏 for cut, 👐 for release.

We need the light to be yellow when wire 3 (green) is cut. The manual states the light walks a circle of five colours every round. It was yellow in Round 1 and blue in Round 2. Therefore, yellow will recur in Round 6 (and every 5th round thereafter: Round 1, 6, 11...). 

Right now it is Round 3, so the light is not yellow. Blind must wait and not cut any wire. We should send NO/WAIT (`👎`) to Deaf so Deaf can instruct Blind to wait, while sending nothing to Blind so Blind does not mistake blanks for wire indices.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Standing by. Deaf will see your gesture this round and tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute again gestured NO / WAIT (👎). Blind, remember Mute hears everything you say! If you are asking Mute questions or holding a button, Mute is answering NO / WAIT. BOMB STATUS: Light is now [WHITE] (was yellow -> blue -> white). Display is [0]. Wires: 1:[blue], 2:[red], 3:[green]. MUTE: If you need to give specific instructions to Blind, use: 🤏 + (☝/✌/🤟) = cut wire 1/2/3; 👉 = tap button; ✊ = hold button; 👐 = release button; 👍 = YES; 👎 = NO/WAIT.

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Note that there are NO buttons on the bomb. My only possible action is cutting wire 1, 2, or 3. If you are waiting for a specific light color or display number reported by Deaf, whenever the time is right, gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (1, 2, or 3), and Deaf will call it out to me.
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute gestured NO / DO NOT RELEASE (👎). Current bomb state: Light is now [RED]. Display is [0]. Wires are intact: 1:[blue], 2:[red], 3:[green]. MUTE: If Blind is holding a button or waiting for a specific color/moment, gesture 👍 the instant Blind should release or act! Gesture 👎 if Blind must continue waiting.

The defusal manual specifies that the green wire must be cut when the light is yellow. The light follows a strict cycle of 5 colors every round:
- Round 1: Yellow
- Round 2: Blue
- Round 3: White
- Round 4: Red
- Round 5: (5th color)
- Round 6: Yellow

Wire 3 is green. Therefore, wire 3 must be cut during Round 6 when the light returns to yellow.

Since the turn order in every round is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf:
- Deaf speaks at the end of the round, so any instruction Deaf speaks in Round 5 will be heard by Blind at the beginning of Round 6.
- In Round 6, Blind will act and cut wire 3 while the light is yellow.

We must not gesture to Blind this round, as that would cause Blind to cut prematurely in Round 5. Signaling Deaf with `🤏` and `🤟` instructs Deaf to tell Blind to cut wire 3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Understood, waiting for your signal. When the right condition is met, gesture cut and the wire number (1, 2, or 3) to Deaf so Deaf can tell me.
Deaf says: BLIND: MUTE SAYS CUT WIRE 3! Cut the third wire now! Bomb status: Light is now [PURPLE], display is [0]. Wires: 1:blue, 2:red, 3:green. Cut wire 3!

The light cycle runs through five colors:
1. Yellow (Round 1)
2. Blue (Round 2)
3. White (Round 3)
4. Red (Round 4)
5. Purple (Round 5)
6. Yellow (Round 6)

In Round 6, the light has rotated back to yellow. The manual specifies: "The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut. light: yellow -> cut wire color: green". Wire 3 is green.

At the end of Round 5, Deaf instructed Blind: "BLIND: MUTE SAYS CUT WIRE 3! Cut the third wire now!". Blind takes their turn immediately following Mute in Round 6 while the light is yellow. To ensure Blind cuts wire 3 without hesitation, I will also send 3 gestures directly to Blind (as Blind requested: 3 gestures = 3 blanks = cut wire 3) and confirm with Deaf.

```
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
